did_you_know.text: The first verse presents two names for God—“Most High” and “Shaddai”—and describes the protected person with two images: dwelling in the “secret place” and taking shelter under God’s “shadow”.
In this verse, the speaker personally declares his faith: the LORD is his “refuge” and “fortress.” These words evoke both a place of safety and a stronghold that protects from danger.
Divine protection is pictured as wings: the person takes refuge under them, while “shield and buckler” represent protective armor. The verse connects this protection with the LORD’s “faithfulness.”

The verse presents threats that appear at different times: the “terror by night” is contrasted with the arrow that flies “by day.” In this way, it describes protection that is not limited to any particular hour.

The dangers are also described by the time they appear: pestilence works “in darkness,” while “destruction”—a term describing a deadly attack—strikes at noon. The contrast emphasizes the dangers of both day and night.

The numbers “a thousand” and “ten thousand” describe a massive downfall around the person, yet the verse emphasizes that the harm does not reach him. It is a poetic picture of extraordinary protection.

This verse returns to the opening idea: the LORD is the refuge, and the person has made the “Most High” his dwelling place. The repetition connects the person’s trust with his symbolic dwelling with God.
According to the verse, the LORD commands his angels to guard the person “in all your ways.” The emphasis is on protection throughout all his journeys, not only in one particular place.

The verse uses images of dangerous animals—the lion, cobra, young lion, and serpent—to describe overcoming danger. It is not describing an actual struggle, but uses poetic language of victory and protection.

In this verse, the speaker changes: the LORD speaks in the first person and promises to rescue the one who “holds fast” to him and knows his name. The chapter concludes with a series of promises: answering in times of trouble, delivering, honoring, granting long life, and providing salvation.
